arion.name: Arion, Tyrant of the Emerald Wrath

arion_ravager.name: Arion, Tyrant of the Emerald Wrath
arion_ravager.notes: Mounted Arion (Ravager) form. Scale/shadow not read (renderer not inspected for this extra).

bringer_of_doom.name: Bringer Of Doom
bringer_of_doom.notes: Phase 1 entity armageddon_mod:bringer_of_doom; phase 2 is armageddon_mod:bringer_of_doom_p_2 (see bringer_of_doom_p2.json). Glow = BringerOfDoomLayer, RenderType.eyes(bod_texture_glow.png).

bringer_of_doom_p2.name: Bringer Of Doom
bringer_of_doom_p2.notes: Phase 2 of the Bringer of Doom. Glow = BringerOfDoomP2Layer, RenderType.eyes(bod_texture_glow.png) - the mod reuses the phase-1 glow texture although bod_p2_texture is 256x256 (glow is 128x128): UVs normalise, so the glow lands at half scale; render it only if it looks right. bringer_of_doom_p2.animation.json has no walk animation.

eldorath.name: Eldorath the Ancient Builder
eldorath.notes: Model file is geo/eldorathbeard.geo.json (EldoraththeAncientBuilderModel); geo/eldorathrelic* are relic blocks.

ender_dragon.name: Ender Dragon

animNames.idle: DragonModel.renderToBuffer flap cycle, level flight (Java code, as molang)

ender_dragon.notes: Bedrock geometry.dragon has no neck/tail bones (the engine instantiates neck1-5/tail1-12), so the model is rebuilt from the Java 1.20.1 EnderDragonRenderer.createBodyLayer parts with the 5 neck and 12 tail segments laid out exactly as DragonModel.renderToBuffer does for straight, level flight (no turning/pitch: getLatencyPos deltas = 0, getHeadPartYOffset = 0). Bind pose = flap fraction 0. Idle = the renderToBuffer flap formulas (jaw, wings, wing tips, legs, neck/tail undulation, body bob) as molang; flap speed 0.02857/tick (EnderDragon.aiStep 0.2/(0.6*10+1) at 0.6 blocks/tick cruise) -> 1.750s per beat. Omitted: the renderer-level translate(0,f1-2,-3) blocks and translate(0,0,1)/yaw (placement only); only the time-varying part of the bob is animated. Texture = Java dragon.png; the Bedrock sample (textures/entity/dragon/dragon.tga) has identical RGB but a different alpha mask on 3922 pixels, so the Java file is used.

goblin_lord.name: The Goblin Lord
goblin_lord.notes: Entity class uses animation.gobelinlord.walk2 for walking (walk is unused).

nyxaris.name: Nyxaris, the Veil of Oblivion
nyxaris.notes: Nyxaris reuses the "khyrossshadow" GeckoLib model. Glow = NyxarisTheVeilOfOblivionLayer (RenderType.eyes). Texture has 1 semi-transparent pixels -> alpha blend.

sanghor_p2.notes: Texture has 3 semi-transparent pixels -> alpha blend.

warden.name: Warden
warden.notes: geo = Bedrock geometry.warden (bedrock-samples). Cross-checked against Java WardenModel.createBodyLayer (fdr): identical pivots/cubes/uv/mirror. Texture taken from the Java 1.20.1 client jar; pixel-identical to the Bedrock warden.png. Bedrock animations are molang-driven by engine queries (modified_distance_moved, heartbeat...), so idle/walk are the Java WardenModel formulas written as molang (life_time based). Layers: bioluminescent (alpha 1) on head/arms/legs, pulsating spots alpha max(0,cos(age*0.045)*0.25) (+pi for spots_2) on body/head/arms/legs, per WardenRenderer/WardenModel part lists. Heart and tendril layers omitted (only visible on heartbeat/vibration).

wither.name: Wither

animNames.idle: WitherBossModel.setupAnim ribcage/tail bob (Java code, as molang)

wither.notes: geo built from the Java WitherBossModel.createBodyLayer (bytecode constants) because the Bedrock geometry.witherBoss (format 1.8.0) uses a different bone layout (upperBodyPart1-3/head1-3, tail positioned by molang). Cube origins/sizes/uv were checked to match the Bedrock file (shoulders, ribs, heads). Texture from the Java client jar, pixel-identical to Bedrock wither.png. In game the model is drawn at scale 2.0; heads track the target (not animated here).
